I really don’t have the words to fully explain how much this place helped me. It’s just something you feel when you’re there. The program has real depth, nothing fake, nothing rushed. They actually take time to understand you and your situation.

Every person I met here truly cared. The counselors, nurses, kitchen staff, support team, everyone. You can tell they are not just doing a job. They want to help people who are hurting. I came in thinking my case was too complicated and that no rehab could really help me. I was wrong.

After a little over two months, I left feeling more stable, clearer in my mind, and honestly happier than I’ve been in years. I got my life back. This place doesn’t give you shortcuts or quick comfort. You are expected to do the work, but you are never alone while doing it.

If you want real healing and not just to be “treated,” this is the place. I’m very thankful for everything they did for me. I won’t forget it.

We were recommended The Cabin Chiang Mai for help with our son’s depression and addiction, and we honestly can’t recommend them enough. He is back home now and doing really well.

The staff were caring and professional throughout, and communication with our family was excellent from start to finish. The family programme was especially valuable — it educated us, supported us, and helped keep us sane during a very difficult time.

We’re incredibly grateful for the care and support we all received.

I cannot not express how incredible this program is. Substance. One word to describe The Cabin. The staff, the program, the food, the way they individualize care . THE VALUE. I’ve never felt such a return on an investment in my life. They have world class counselors that are able to unlock the individual enigma that each addict presents. I’m brought to tears of gratitude just writing this bc of the love and energy that they chose to put into their clients. From the nurses, cooks, support staff, yoga/reiki, art teachers to counselors. They all are there bc they want to help those that are suffering. 14 of last 18 years I spent on a combination of Heroin/fentanyl or methadone. I felt no rehab could handle a situation as complex as mine. I left after 8.5 weeks with my happiness back, my emotional stability back, my life back... If you want to be pampered and have your every desire for instant gratification met this may not be the place for you. If you want to do the real work that leads to recovery, to be held accountable, while being provided every opportunity to heal then this is the place for you. Thank you all for your commitment and unwavering dedication to my recovery. I’ll never forget you.

I am a registered nurse from Australia, and my family and I sent my brother to The Cabin due to it's long-standing reputation as a safe, ethical, and well-run rehabilitation facility. We believed we were sending him somewhere that prioritised client safety and accurately represented its practices. Unfortunately, this was not the case.

It became apparent that The Cabin is now operating under new ownership, benefiting from its former reputation while no longer upholding the standards it once advertised. Prior to my brother’s admission, I had a consultation with Elijah, who explicitly stated that clients were never taken off-site unsupervised and that clients could not access other clients’ rooms.

During my brother’s stay, he attended an AA meeting where clients were taken off-site without supervision. One client absconded, later returned for transport back to the facility, and then entered and trashed my brother’s room. Cigarette butts were placed inside my brother’s hat, cigarettes were thrown across the floor, his bathroom was torn apart, his clothes were scattered throughout the room, wooden boxes were overturned, and his personal recovery notes were ripped apart. This was an incredibly violating and distressing experience.

My brother was extremely distressed and did not sleep that night, fearful of what may have happened due to staff’s inability to safely manage another client. Other clients were also visibly frightened, reportedly locking their doors with belts in an attempt to feel safe. Despite requesting counselling support following this incident, my brother was denied access to support.

My brother was the first to inform me of what had occurred, followed by an email from his therapist stating that he had “credible reason to leave.” As his family, on the other side of the world, this was an awful and helpless feeling. The way staff interacted with our family throughout this event was emotionless, insensitive, and lacking compassion, which only compounded the distress.

Given the seriousness of the incident and the misleading information provided to us regarding supervision and safety, we made the decision to remove my brother from the facility. I was blown away by the unprofessional manner in which The Cabin handled this situation.

When I escalated the matter to the CEO after requesting my brother be discharged, he attempted to instil fear by stating, “You know he can access weed anywhere here.” This was an entirely inappropriate and unprofessional response.

My brother was at the facility for 16 days of a 6-week program, which we had paid for in full. Despite the discharge being a direct result of The Cabin’s negligence and failure to provide the safety they advertised, no refund was offered for the remaining weeks or even for the compromised portion of his stay.

I cannot emphasise enough that I would not recommend this rehab. It has changed significantly since changing ownership, and families should be extremely cautious. Please do not trust this facility with your vulnerable family members.

I know someone who stayed there Sept. - Oct. 2025 and they came out a totally reinvigorated person with a new found resolve to stay sober and with new found tools to help them accomplish their goals. I was very impressed with the program, the facilities, and the competence and compassion of the staff - top to bottom. Thank God for the Cabin and I recommend it highly.

WARNING! I would NOT recommend the Cabin to anyone! Complete BREACH of Service Standards, Duty of Care and Safety Policies.
I attended rehabilitation at The Cabin in September 2025. The Cabin still is withholding $39,650. Dismissing the events trying to cover it up!
6 clients were dropped off to an AA park meeting. One of the clients took off and went missing for the entire meeting. Apparently ‘normal’ for him to do so. He returned in time to catch the lift back to the Cabin. He was completely off his face, unable to speak, passing out and couldn’t keep he’s eyes open.
Given water, he rinsed his mouth out and spat the water out. Returning to the cabin the client went straight to the sink to rinse, he’s mouth out again. I asked staff to check on him as I was worried about him overdosing.
Later, the client was caught naked swimming in the fishpond. Staff denied the client being under the influence of drugs LYING and saying the test was negative. That evening he was moved to a different room with a high balcony despite reports being made he stated he was now feeling suicidal. At this point I was really worried about him. I didn’t think placing someone there with suicidal ideation was a good idea, he could have jumped off the balcony.
This client repeatedly stated that he was forced to be here and could not wait get back on substances.
Sunday Morning, he was below my villa.
I later returned and found he had entered my room and left a note on my desk and cigarette butts at my door. People were scared and locking their doors with belts.
Later that day, walking back to show a support worker the Cigarette butts and the note. He was in my room! There were loud banging noises. He had put cigarette butts in my hat, threw them all over the floor, tore my bathroom apart, put my clothes on the floor, wooden boxes had been thrown around, cosmetics all over the room. Personal education notes ripped up and thrown around.
It was confirmed to me and a fellow client that it was true that the client was on drugs. This had been confirmed by a Cabin Support Staff member to us! The rest of the staff lied and tried to cover it all up!
When my family selected The Cabin Chiang Mai, they relied on the representations made in the brochure, on the website, and by staff, which promised:
•    Careful screening of clients for suitability to ensure a safe environment.
•    24-hour supervision and medical support.
•    No access to drugs or alcohol.
•    Professionally managed and supervised offsite excursions.
•    Private, secure accommodation and a safe environment conducive to recovery.

These standards were not met during my stay. Another client, who openly stated they were unwilling to engage in rehabilitation, gained access to substances while unsupervised offsite. This same client later acted aggressively towards myself, entering my private room, trashing it and destroying my personal belongings. Despite these serious breaches, the client was not discharged, supervised, or monitored as required under The Cabin’s stated policy.

I was left without access to counselling support when I requested it and was provided no assurance of safety following the incident. The facility’s failure to implement security measures or maintain communication with my family caused significant emotional distress and placed my mental health and recovery at serious risk.

These events represent:
•    Negligence in ensuring client safety and duty of care.
•    Breach of contract as the services provided did not align with those advertised and agreed upon.
•    Misleading conduct under Thailand’s Consumer Protection Act, which prohibits false or misleading representations and entitles consumers to refunds where services are substandard or misrepresented.

Due to these failures, my family made the decision to remove me from The Cabin, as I no longer felt safe or supported. The experience caused me significant emotional distress, high stress levels for my immediate family and a financial loss for the family.

text:
The Cabin is a sad shadow of a place profiting from its past glories and past reputation.  They were incompetent right from the admissions process where they are supposed to do a thorough examination of each new victims possessions when they first check in. This was supposedly done in the interest of everyone’s safety. Well, it is not a safe place because they overlooked a 15inch laptop in the luggage.
They also are very careless with medical reports and other confidential info concerning their victims. They sent very private and confidential information concerning their victim’s condition to a wrong email address and when they realized their mistake they didn’t even offer an apology.
Their incompetent staff then escalated the laptop issue, making false claims and pushing their mistakes onto the victim who lost his cool and walked out of the glorified resort.
They do not understand that people who go to places like this are very stressed and basically desperate for help. They go through the motions to treat their victims but ultimately profit is all they care about. Beware of this place.

I would give this rehab zero stars if I could. Based on my family members experience, the centre falls far short of providing real support for recovery. Communication is poor, promises are often not kept, and feedback is treated dismissively. Overall, it feels more like a business than a place genuinely invested in helping people get clean.

One of my best friends went to The Cabin for help with a cocaine addiction, and honestly, the change has been amazing. Before going, things were really rough, he was in a bad place and nothing seemed to help. But after his time at The Cabin, he came back a totally different person in the best way possible.

The support he got there was exactly what he needed. He always talks about how understanding and professional the team was, and how the program actually helped him figure out what was going on and how to deal with it.

It’s been so good to have my friend back; clear-headed, focused, and actually happy again. Super grateful to The Cabin for giving him that reset. If you’re thinking about it for someone you care about, this place really works.

As someone who has been in treatment in the United States 6+ times and now significant experience working in the international treatment industry.. I can say that the Cabin is one of a kind. With a strong clinical team, an incredible hospitality team and a beautiful physical setting they truly provide an excellent experience for their patients. One thing I look for in a facility is the culture and community which are both very much established and thriving at the Cabin. Sudi, Lee and Phil operate this facility with laser sharp focus and a high ethical standard. They protect the ethos and quality of treatment they provide at all costs.

I had been looking around for some time for a rehab for a close family member. We spoke to many different rehabs in Chiang Mai and The Cabin was the clear choice. The communication was excellent and the process was smooth putting my family member at ease straight away.
We cannot thank the team enough for their work. I have personally seen a wonderful transformation in them and they very much enjoyed the programme, the meals, the group and 1-1 sessions as well as the stunning grounds!
We can’t thank The Cabin enough!

I have not been a guest of The Cabin, thus this review makes no comment on their facilities or services.

However I did reach out to The Cabin on behalf of a friend in need of effective treatment.

The Cabin are very forthcoming when it comes to self-promotion, and yet the Cabin has a strict policy of non-disclosure when it comes to the effectiveness of their treatments.

They claim on their website: "Five thousand treatments completed.
Five thousand lives changed.
Five thousand stories rewritten."

However if you ask The Cabin to support that claim with any data they will refuse to do so.  In fact they would not even confirm that they had such data.

If you value transparency and accountability, then you should look elsewhere.

Rehab clinics should be transparent and accountable regarding their outcomes for several reasons. Firstly, it allows patients and their families to make informed decisions about their treatment options. By providing accurate and comprehensive information about their success rates and treatment methods, rehab clinics can help patients select the most appropriate program to meet their needs.

Secondly, transparency and accountability can help to promote quality improvement in the rehab industry. By tracking and reporting outcomes, clinics can identify areas where they need to improve and implement changes to enhance their effectiveness. This can lead to better treatment outcomes for patients and contribute to the overall improvement of the rehab industry.

Finally, being transparent and accountable can help to build trust with patients, families, and the wider community. When rehab clinics are open and honest about their outcomes and practices, they demonstrate a commitment to providing the best possible care and outcomes for their patients. This can help to build a positive reputation and attract more patients to their services in the future.

If The Cabin's management choose to respond to this review, please explain why The Cabin is unwilling to support its glowing sales pitch with any data? Why be evasive with regards to your track record?   Do you think transparency and accountability should be amongst The Cabin's value?

The Cabin took very good care of a family member recently. He has just returned home after 6 weeks in their care and is re-adjusted, full of positivity and looks the healthiest I have seen him look in years. I’m very happy to recommend The Cabin and their life changing (and saving) treatment programme.

This is THE place to go to when you are struggling with addiction and/or mental health issues. All the people at the CABIN have one purpose and that is to meet you where you are in your process (mentally, physically, emotionally) and help you  move forward. Very experienced, state of the art, caring professionals who work from a holistic approach that really     creates change if you are willing to do the work. The family program that they offer for loved ones is an amazing support system where education on what addiction is and how to deal with it, and how to navigate yourself when someone around you is suffering from addiction, is so helpful. Dont doubt, sign up today. Get the help you need. All you have to do is send an email or call. You got this.

I have known about the quality of treatment delivered at The Cabin Chiang Mai for a long time. Therefore, I was delighted to visit recently and see for myself. I was very impressed with the facility, team and program they deliver.

Being a clinician in addiction services, I throughly enjoy working with The Cabin Chiang Mai. They have flawless processes in place starting from admission to treatment and then aftercare services. Their treatment program is trauma Informed Practice and has been prepared with a lot of care and consideration keeping in mind the complexity of addiction. They understand that recovery at an inpatient is only the beginning and link clients to professionals best suited to their needs in their hometown. They also run continuing care groups which have been hugely beneficial to long-term clients. I have faith in the work they do and would highly recommend them to anyone looking for long-term changes.

The Cabin has reopened under new management and staffing. It offers a wide variety of programs with specialized expertise in each. These are expected to raise the standard from historical experiences. In addition, an internationally renowned group of healthcare leaders, clinicians and researchers have been added to the Medical Advisory Board with an emphasis on quality and safety. Look for great outcomes in the future.

The counselling staff are among the best I've ever been in contact with. I've seen many psychologists and counsellors and the Cabins are by far the best.

I found a lot of use from the art therapy with Yuliya. She has a way of getting information and emotions out with just a few scribbles on a page.

I learnt about "box breathing" during meditation sessions with Nim. It came in handy for many situations, from solo meditation to controlling my anxiety in so many circumstances. Nim is a wealth of knowledge when it comes to engaging with life's trials and tribulations.

The support staff are great. And a barrel of laughs too.
The nurses are very caring.
Don't forget to meet Prem and Mickey in the restaurant area. They're great for a chat and always have a smile on their face.

I definitely recommend learning some basic Thai so you can chat with the lovely cleaning staff, gardener's and security.

Be prepared to get fit with Aon and Nay in the gym too.

Yoga in the morning with Nock and Siri is a great way to stretch after a good night's sleep.

The Cabins new addition Prijanka who does meditation and mindfulness sessions, is out of this world.
Prijanka helped me to see myself in a different light. I suffer from severe self esteem issues which go way back to childhood trauma. And these sessions have helped me immensely.

"A leader is one that knows the way, goes the way, shows the way" and the management team of The Cabin are leaders that know the way, go the way and show the way. Their vision, mission, their committment, their values speak for themselves. The drive of The Cabin's management team is to make a difference, to support life changes of the residents during and beyond their stay. Kudos!!

I have referred many clients to The Cabin. Their Clinical Programme is exceptional and delivered by highly qualified Staff. Most clients experience huge transformations and build strong foundations for lasting recovery.

Pretty facilities, unbelievably bad administration. I do not recommend The Cabin unless you happen to be local, DO NOT TRAVEL from afar to attend this rehab facility. They failed to pick up our family member at the airport causing hours of distress. No apologies, no explanation, no reimbursement. Highly do not recommend sending your loved one to such a shoddy run place.

Abuse of a substance or addictive behavior is a complicated subject, however, it seems to always be underpinned by a cause, stressor, event, life circumstance that triggers self abusive behavior. The Cabin, as it was pre COVID, appeared to …

When I contacted them a year ago for my father we talked a lot until i asked a question about insurance then they stopped responding. Still needing help i contacted them recently and was talking a lot until i again asked about insurance then they stopped responding. They will probably help on the insurance side a bit but any sign this is a dependency of yours and they'll cut off communication. While this doesn't matter for most people who can self-finance, what this IS representative of is a facility that has been set up to help people in need but where profit is the first and foremost consideration. Their values and moral standing are  bankrupt. Even if you're financially strong, you do not want the help of an institution that has the moral compass to ignore someone who has come to them for help because there are signs they have some financial dependencies, how about suggesting alternatives or, ya know, doing some basic admin work to get the insurance approvals sorted? For the record, I am absolutely able to finance my dad's treatment myself, but if my insurance covers it why would i not utilise that channel? You people are awful.
Excellent team committed to their stated mission.
I haven't visited them, but I commented here because I want a number to contact them via WhatsApp.
Worse than a boarding school. Rigid, concentration camp actually. Arrogant people
Wonderful space, programme and people ♥️
It’s truly magnificent, a life-changing experience. Thank you, thank you, thank you. Merci beaucoup !!!
I see hope with a bliss of ease...
Good experience healing center
Absolutely fabulous

After having experienced rehab centres in Delhi, India,  this was paradise. The treatment, the immersion in the programme, the counsillors and support staff were simple awesome and went out of their way to answer your needsa and make you feel at home. Initially went for 4 weeks but soon extended for another 2 in order to squeeze out whatever answers i could get. Came back feeling like Paul Newman and with a different world view, and that of myself.  Would recommend this without any hesitation.

The Cabin was right for me. Very comfortable, very competent and friendly team. Very good atmosphere. Peaceful, serene. I felt save and I got from it exactly what I needed. 19 months clean now. I can only recommend it.
The atmosphere is great; it's very close to nature.
